answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08, the proteins genuinely related to histones are the other members of the Histone-fold superfamily, a.22.1, in fold a.22 (Histone-fold), class a (All alpha proteins). Within that superfamily, the curated families are: a.22.1.1 Nucleosome core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, H4, and macro-H2A.1 histone domain); a.22.1.2 Archaeal histone (for example Methanothermus fervidus histones A and B); a.22.1.3 TBP-associated factors, TAFs (for example TAF(II)-135/hTAF4 and TAF(II)-20/hTAF12 histone-fold domains, plus a histone domain of Son of sevenless); and a.22.1.4 Bacterial histone-fold protein. A fifth family, a.22.1.0 'automated matches', is not a curated grouping and should not be treated as evidence. The shared histone fold (a pair of helix-loop-helix motifs that dimerize as a handshake) is the basis for the superfamily-level relationship. Family-level divergence is the appropriate evolutionary strength for the nucleosome core histones versus the archaeal histones versus the TAFs. Classes and folds above the superfamily (a and a.22) are too coarse to imply a relationship on their own. Limits: SCOPe's superfamily grouping is an expert-curated homology claim, not a sequence-identity statement, so specific pairs (e.g., an archaeal histone and H3) should not be assumed to have close sequence similarity. Function does not transfer across families just because they share the fold; TAFs are part of TFIID, not nucleosomes. Several other entries returned by name search are not histone relatives in SCOPe: linker histones H1/H5 (a.4.5.13, Linker histone H1/H5 family in the winged-helix superfamily a.4.5, fold a.4) use a different fold; the bacterial H-NS histone-like proteins (a.155.1, fold a.155) are a different fold; the Histone H3 C-terminal fragment entries (j.63.1) are peptide-like fragments, not histone-fold domains; and the histone-modifying enzymes (HDAC c.42.1.2, p300 d.108.1.11, SET7/9 b.76.2.1 and b.85.7.1, Dot1l c.66.1.31) act on histones but are unrelated folds. These are functional or name-based associations, not homology. Caveats: this is release 2.08 (frozen 2021-07-28, with a periodic update dated 2026-08-16 that I did not query); I did not inspect domain-level structure or sequence hits for representative selection, so the answer rests on the classification tree and name search rather than on any structure alignment; and no SID-level domain representatives were checked.
